svg.title: Figure 4. Shear deformation
svg.desc: Two panels. (a) A beam segment deforms in two ways: in bending its cross-sections rotate but stay normal to the axis; in shear they slide past each other, so the axis tilts by the shear strain gamma equal to f s V over GA. The deflection is the sum of the two. (b) Log-log plot of the total deflection divided by the bending-only deflection against span-to-depth ratio for a simply supported beam with a central load, for a rectangle and for a typical I-section, Poisson's ratio 0.3. Both curves approach 1 for long spans and rise steeply for short ones; the I-section's curve lies well above the rectangle's, so it needs a longer span before shear falls below 5 percent of the deflection, marked by a horizontal line.
